section_summary: This section records U.S. interdepartmental decisions and proposals to expand foreign banks’ services in occupied Japan, including trade banking, remittances, yen loans, property restitution, and foreign currency drafts. It also covers Italian and French yen balances affected by Japanese bank reorganization, correspondence about Bank of Japan accounting, and a draft response to proposed Japanese banking laws.

people.name: Roswell H. Whitman
people.role: Acting associate chief, Division of Occupied Areas

people.name: Charles E. Saltzman
people.role: SANACC chairman and Assistant Secretary of State

people.name: Edwin M. Martin
people.role: Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs

subfiles.title: Establishment of Commercial and Foreign Trade Banking Facilities in Japan
subfiles.about: Recommends wider authority for foreign bank branches to serve SCAP and foreign private traders.
subfiles.summary: The study proposes admitting qualified foreign banks and licensing normal commercial and export-import services under SCAP controls, while excluding local services to Japanese nationals. Its factual and discussion appendices describe earlier restrictions, SCAP’s request, equal treatment of banks, and logistical limits on new branches.

subfiles.title: SCAP request to expand foreign bank functions
subfiles.about: Requests delegated authority to expand foreign banking facilities as Japanese trade revives.
subfiles.summary: SCAP seeks flexibility to amend bank licenses without repeated Washington approval.

subfiles.title: War Department proposal on foreign bank functions
subfiles.about: Seeks SCAP’s views on trade banking, new branches, and applications by American banks.
subfiles.summary: The department proposes allowing foreign banks to hold export proceeds and serve private traders. It outlines Federal Reserve screening of American branch applications and requests SCAP’s assessment of banking needs and the National City Bank’s Tokyo operations.

subfiles.title: Trade mission cable on bank entry
subfiles.to: Secretary of State and War Department
subfiles.about: Urges immediate permission for U.S. and other foreign banks to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The mission asks for prompt processing so bank personnel can enter and trade banking can begin.

subfiles.title: SCAP concurrence on expanded foreign bank functions
subfiles.about: Concurs with expanded banking proposals and recommends a Chase National Bank branch in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: SCAP supports the proposal, subject to final approval of applications in theater.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable on commercial and foreign trade banking
subfiles.about: Drafts authority and a public announcement for foreign bank branches in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The cable would authorize foreign banks to provide trade and private trader services under SCAP regulations. Its proposed announcement stresses equal treatment and physical limits on the number of branches.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SWNCC and SANACC documents to Nanking
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: Encloses coordinating committee documents for the embassy.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SWNCC and SANACC documents and notes the committee’s renamed title.

subfiles.title: Forwarding SWNCC 226/9
subfiles.about: Forwards approved remittance policy and requests notification and a press release.
subfiles.summary: Requests Far Eastern Commission notice, press release, and copies of implementation.

subfiles.title: Decision amending SWNCC 226/9
subfiles.about: Directs replacement of a revised page in the remittance policy paper.
subfiles.summary: Records approval as amended and directs holders to replace page 77.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 226/9 circulation note
subfiles.about: Circulates a State Member statement on remittances between the United States and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Submits the enclosed statement for committee consideration.

subfiles.title: Reestablishment of Remittance Facilities Between the United States and Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes opening commercial remittances to anyone in Japan, including Japanese nationals.
subfiles.summary: The statement reviews earlier limits, changed regulations, and SCAP’s conditional agreement. It recommends remittances to any person in Japan subject to SCAP rules.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable on remittances to Japan
subfiles.about: Implements broader eligibility for remittances through American bank branches.
subfiles.summary: Permits remittances to any person in Japan under SCAP limits and specifies outpayment arrangements.

subfiles.title: Proposed press release on remittances to Japan
subfiles.about: Announces broader remittance access and describes payment limits and currencies.
subfiles.summary: The release states that anyone in Japan may receive bank remittances, generally up to $1,000 monthly, with SCAP able to authorize more. It explains yen and dollar facility payments and says other financial controls remain in force.

subfiles.title: Notice to U.S. Member of the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Requests advance notice to commission members of the remittance policy announcement.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SWNCC 226/9 and asks the member to inform other delegates.

subfiles.title: Forwarding second decision amending SWNCC 226/4
subfiles.about: Forwards the second decision amending the earlier remittance policy.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of the decision.

subfiles.title: Approval of SWNCC 226/4
subfiles.about: Reports approval of the original policy restoring remittance facilities.
subfiles.summary: Records approval and requests Treasury licensing and transmission of the implementing cable.

subfiles.title: Second decision amending SWNCC 226/4
subfiles.about: Directs replacement of the policy’s remittance eligibility page.
subfiles.summary: Records committee approval and directs substitution of revised page 25.

subfiles.title: Revised page 25 of SWNCC 226/4
subfiles.about: Sets the revised rules for commercial remittances to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Opens remittances to any person in Japan under SCAP rules.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of SWNCC 226/9 to Nanking
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Nanking
subfiles.about: Encloses the approved remittance policy for embassy information.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SWNCC 226/9 and notes the reference paper is unavailable.

subfiles.title: Request for comments on foreign bank functions
subfiles.about: Requests comments on a State working paper about expanding foreign bank functions.
subfiles.summary: Circulates a discussion draft and asks for prompt comments to Parke.

subfiles.title: Expansion of Functions of Foreign Banks in Japan
subfiles.to: State, Army, and Treasury working group
subfiles.about: Evaluates proposed additional services for licensed foreign bank branches in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The draft recommends restoring prewar deposits and safe custody items, allowing limited yen loans and foreign currency drafts, and letting banks represent foreign claimants and transmit securities orders. It would defer investment in Japanese government obligations pending broader policy. Its appendices review earlier authority, SCAP requests, and safeguards against domestic banking competition and foreign exchange misuse.

subfiles.title: SCAP cable on return of prewar deposits
subfiles.about: Recommends return of prewar yen deposits and safe custody items to foreign banks.
subfiles.summary: Seeks removal of license restrictions obstructing restitution to United Nations nationals.

subfiles.title: War Department inquiry on expanded bank activities
subfiles.about: Seeks details about restored deposits and proposed yen lending by foreign banks.
subfiles.summary: Washington asks whether restored deposits would be regulated like Japanese bank accounts and seeks loan sources, repayment terms, and purposes. It raises concerns about domestic banking competition, exchange controls, and inflation.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on deposits and yen loans
subfiles.about: Explains how restored deposits and restricted yen loans would operate.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says restored accounts would permit withdrawals only and estimates 30 million yen across roughly 3,300 depositors. It proposes loans to licensed concerns with yen income for approved operating costs, arguing this would ease pressure on Japanese bank credit.

subfiles.title: SCAP proposal for yen loans
subfiles.about: Asks whether existing authority permits foreign banks to lend yen to licensed concerns.
subfiles.summary: Requests guidance on a controlled yen loan plan for operating expenses.

subfiles.title: SCAP proposal for bank drafts
subfiles.about: Recommends permitting foreign banks to sell drafts for authorized foreign payments.
subfiles.summary: Says transfers and travelers’ checks do not meet all payment needs.

subfiles.title: War Department inquiry on drafts and bank functions
subfiles.about: Requests safeguards for drafts and a complete review of desired foreign bank functions.
subfiles.summary: Asks who could buy drafts, how negotiability would be limited, and what further services SCAP seeks.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply on drafts and additional functions
subfiles.about: Identifies draft buyers and proposes further foreign bank services.
subfiles.summary: SCAP proposes dollar and sterling drafts for occupation personnel and licensed traders, with reporting of larger sales. It also requests authority for yen loans, restitution work, securities orders, and investment in Japanese government obligations.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable conveying SANACC conclusions
subfiles.about: Drafts a cable to convey conclusions on foreign bank functions.
subfiles.summary: Contains references and a placeholder for the conclusions text.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Bank of Japan accounting terms
subfiles.about: Asks what two domestic exchange items mean in a Bank of Japan statement.
subfiles.summary: Requests definitions of settled exchange liabilities and unsettled advances.

subfiles.title: Reply on Bank of Japan accounting terms
subfiles.about: Offers a tentative interpretation of two Bank of Japan domestic exchange entries.
subfiles.summary: Suggests the entries concern interbank transfers and cautions that the interpretation is uncertain.

subfiles.title: Approval of proposed bank functions cable
subfiles.about: Approves an agreed cable expanding foreign bank functions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Confirms State approval and agrees the cable may go to SCAP without Far Eastern Commission referral.

subfiles.title: Request for approval of bank functions cable
subfiles.about: Requests prompt approval of a cable authorizing additional bank functions.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a State, Treasury, and Army working draft for SCAP.

subfiles.title: Italian and French Yen Balances
subfiles.about: Reviews Italian and French accounts reduced during Japanese bank reorganization.
subfiles.summary: Explains the earlier dispute over account classification and proposes reopening the question of residual balances.

subfiles.title: Draft cable on Italian and French yen balances
subfiles.about: Suggests release of residual Italian and French yen balances.
subfiles.summary: Asks SCAP for a decision following completion of Japanese bank reorganization.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Italian Embassy about yen balances
subfiles.about: Clarifies whether Italy seeks release of residual balances or reversal of earlier write-offs.
subfiles.summary: Parke records that the issue may concern immunity from write-offs, rather than access to remaining funds. He withdraws the draft cable while Ortona seeks clarification.

subfiles.title: Accounts of Istcambi with Yokohama Specie Bank
subfiles.about: Recommends protection of one Italian government yen account from wartime trade treatment.
subfiles.summary: Reviews six accounts and argues Account R, funded before wartime trade, may merit release and protected treatment.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable on Italian government accounts
subfiles.about: Proposes treatment of Italian diplomatic, government, and trade accounts.
subfiles.summary: The draft distinguishes Account R and other official funds from accounts tied to wartime trade. It supports immunity for qualifying official funds while accepting liquidation procedures.

subfiles.title: Duplicate proposed cable on Italian government accounts
subfiles.about: Repeats the proposal for treatment of Italian accounts held by Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate draft protecting qualifying official funds while withholding wartime trade balances.

subfiles.title: Request for concurrence on proposed Japanese banking laws
subfiles.from: F. Footer, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Seeks State Department concurrence in a final draft cable on proposed banking laws.
subfiles.summary: Forwards two copies and requests an early response.

subfiles.title: Final draft cable to SCAP on proposed banking laws
subfiles.about: Comments on proposed Japanese banking legislation and Bank of Japan powers.
subfiles.summary: The draft favors an interim program strengthening Bank of Japan control of reserves, supervision, and credit. It comments on bank classifications, cooperative institutions, securities dealings, and interlocking directorates. The document continues beyond page 208.
